title: Send a chat message
subtitle: talk-to-web · walked 2026-11-02 · walk mode · AI request, six stops

features.title: One chat turn, Send to streamed reply
features.overview: Send makes a POST to /generate/text/. The route checks who you are and spends your rate limit before anything streams. The use case builds the prompt and runs the agent, which yields events. The pipe packs each event into an SSE frame (one small text message on an open response), and React adds the text as it arrives.

stops.name: Screen
stops.what: Send calls streamChat with the model, the text and the conversation id. It goes through authorizedFetch, which adds the access token and retries once on a 401.
stops.hands: An HTTP POST with a bearer token and an abort signal.

stops.name: Door
stops.what: FastAPI checks the token (CurrentUserDep) and the body shape. The route checks the model name. Then the use case spends the global budget and your per-user rate limit, the same sliding-window limiter you saw in upload, and runs the input guard. All of this runs before the 200 leaves, so a refusal is a real 429.
stops.hands: A clean GenerateReplyInput, and a stream that has not started yet.

stops.name: Context
stops.what: The config carries facts the model may never choose: owner, thread, and whether you have documents. LangGraph's checkpointer (saves a thread's history between turns) already holds earlier messages, so only this turn's messages go in. That is also why the system prompt goes in only on a new thread. The user message gets a fenced digest of the thread's documents, capped at 6 documents and 200 characters each.
stops.hands: AgentState with only this turn's new messages, plus the config.

stops.name: Loop
stops.what: Summarize trims a long history first. The agent node calls the model. If the model asks for a tool, the tools node runs it and goes back through summarize. route_after_agent stops on a final answer or after 8 tool laps, and a 150 second deadline cancels the whole run.
stops.hands: A stream of payloads that the use case turns into ReplyEvent objects. Nothing here knows about SSE.

stops.name: Pipe
stops.what: to_sse matches each ReplyEvent and writes one frame: data: {json} plus a blank line. The route only packs events here. The use case built them back at Stops 3 and 4. StreamingResponse sends each frame as soon as it exists.
stops.hands: Text frames over one open HTTP response.

stops.name: Screen again
stops.what: It reads chunks, splits on a blank line, and parses each frame. delta adds text, tool shows a chip, error and done end the loop.
stops.hands: Events to useChat, which updates React state, so the message grows on screen.

features.failure: Prompt injection through an uploaded PDF. The document digest is fenced as untrusted content before it reaches the prompt (generate_reply.py, _documents_note), so the model reads it as data, not orders.
features.choice: The rate limit runs before the stream starts. __call__ is awaited by the route, so a refusal is a real 429. Inside the stream it could only cut off a reply that already sent 200.
features.number: 150 seconds: chat_reply_timeout_seconds in settings.py:130, the deadline for one whole reply.
